newsitem.title: INDIA: Head of India's failed CRB group in police custody.
newsitem.headline: Head of India's failed CRB group in police custody.

text.p: An Indian financier whose CRB group of companies failed last month, throwing into uncertainty the fate of many depositors' investments, has been remanded to the custody of India's federal police, officials said on Tuesday.
Bombay judge B.S. Dhumal directed the country's Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) to hold Chain Roop Bhansali, head of the failed CRB group of companies, until June 24, CBI officials said.
Earlier, Bhansali's lawyer told Dhumal that Bhansali wanted to cooperate with the investigation, and was not seeking bail. But the lawyer denied the CBI allegations against Bhansali.
Two weeks ago the CBI said it would complete within a month an investigation into the group, whose liabilities are estimated at 9.32 billion rupees ($260 million).

Bhansali fled to Hong Kong on May 13 along with his family, after one of India's leading banks, the State Bank of India, complained to the CBI about the firm defaulting on repayment of a 570-million-rupee loan.
He was arrested soon after he flew back to India on Monday.
The Reserve Bank of India, the central bank, last month charged CRB Capital Markets, which has offices in India and overseas, with a series of irregular activities.

The bank also invited claims from investors of CRB Capital Markets for submission to the official liquidator appointed by a local court. A winding-up petition filed by the central bank will be heard on July 22.
Bhansali's return to India was made possible by the Indian government's approval last Thursday of an agreement between India and Hong Kong for the surrender of fugitives and offenders.
Last Thursday the CBI arrested four directors of CRB group companies, a finance controller of the group and a close associate of Bhansali.
